thread:
Maria N.: heads-up — EU edge cluster 3 is seeing a surge of keystore calls (Decrypt) that is exhausting conntrack on the privnet NATs and spiking GPU provisioning latency. GPU queueing up to 90s.
Ajay Patel: alert from autoscaler and keystore timeouts? can you paste the logs/metrics?
sre-bot: ALERT: keystore-decrypt-errors EU-edge-3 | 03:12 UTC | rate=820/s | conntrack_used=98% | gw_queue=long | affected_pools=gpu-heavy,gpu-mixed
Maria N.: copying a short sample from the auth proxy logs: `ERROR 503 keystore-decrypt timed out after 12000ms` repeated. Also seeing `conntrack: table full` on nat-gw-12.
Cameron: that explains the OOM-like behavior. conntrack exhaustion will drop NEW connections leading to backpressure — GPUs sit idle waiting for keystore, autoscaler thinks we need more nodes, costs go up.
Kai: temporary mitigation: increase `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` on NATs and enable `nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established` tuning, but that's a cluster-level change and needs rollout. Also rate-limit keystore decrypts per-IP from auth proxy.
Ajay Patel: any quick firewall-level throttles we can flip? maybe block noisy hosts or reduce burst window for the auth-proxy pool?
Cameron: we can add a short-lived firewall rule to drop client IPs with >500 decrypts/min, behind a feature flag in the edge proxy. Low risk and fast.
Maria N.: deployment QA is small, but we need to ensure we don't accidentally blackhole legit traffic. Can we do a canary in EU-edge-3 only?
Kai: yep — canary for 30m on edge-3, thresholds at 500/min with `X-Client-Id` fallback. Also I'll push conntrack bump to 500k on nat-gw-12 as an emergency patch: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=500000`.
Ajay Patel: what's the cost dent if we keep autoscaler triggered? approx extra $/hr?
Cameron: estimate: extra 8 GPUs live for ~1.5h == ~0.8 GPU-hours -> ~ $6–10 immediate, but if it spins up more due to propagation could hit $50/hr. Long tail (audit logs etc) adds egress and storage.
Maria N.: audit logging volume also spiked because every decrypt logs an entry; that's compounding storage/ingest. Can we sample audit logs while we triage?
Kai: we can temporarily enable 10% sampling for decrypt events in EU region. Config change in logging service — low risk.
Ajay Patel: so plan: (1) canary firewall throttle on EU-edge-3 now, (2) bump conntrack on nat-gw-12 as emergency, (3) enable 10% audit sampling for decrypt events, (4) follow-up: implement keystore connection pooling + per-client backoff to avoid bursts, (5) ops to check autoscaler cooldowns.
Maria N.: assigning actions: @Cameron — deploy firewall canary and monitor 15m; @Kai — conntrack bump + logging sample; @Ajay Patel — watch autoscaler and cost dashboard, rollback if cost or errors increase. I'll update incident doc.
Cameron: deploying canary rule now. will post status. :rocket:
Kai: conntrack bumped and logging sampling toggled. NAT conntrack usage back to 55% after 8m.
Cameron: canary reduced decrypt rate from 820/s -> 240/s in canary pool, GPU queueing down to ~4s.
Maria N.: nice work, leave the canary for 1h then expand if stable. we'll schedule a root-cause follow-up to explore keystore throttling and IAM role boundary changes to reduce per-request auth calls.
Ajay Patel: FYI cost watch set, will post if we see >$30 deviation.
Maria N.: thanks team :thumbsup:
